Lecture 9 Attribute Closure Algorithm in R+ RSQLite

Demo 1
```{r}
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
PSTAT132db <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "PSTAT132-db.sqlite")

#Attribute Closure Algorithm in R + RSQLite
#Relations: R(A, B, C, D)
#FDs: F = {A -> B, B -> C, C -> D}
#Questions: What is A+? Is A a superkey?

#Creating the relation R
R_data <- data.frame(
  A = c(1, 2, 3),
  B = c(10, 20, 30),
  C = c(100, 200, 300),
  D = c(1000, 2000, 3000)
)

dbWriteTable(PSTAT132db, "R", R_data, overwrite = TRUE) # writing the R data frame into SQLite as a table called R, replacing an existing table named R if one exists

#Storing the functional dependencies in a table
F_data <- data.frame(
  #left hand side is the determinant, right hand side is the dependent attribute 
  lhs = c("A", "B", "C"),
  rhs = c("B", "C", "D")
)
#Saves the dependency table in SQLite under the name FDs
#Instead of hardcoding each dependency inside the algorithm, we store them in a table. The algorithm can then retrieve the rules and apply them autocomatically
dbWriteTable(PSTAT132db, "FDs", F_data, overwrite = TRUE)

#Defining the attribute closure function
attribute_closure <- function(PSTAT132db, fd_table, start_attrs, all_attrs) #calculates the closure of whichever attributes we provide, and those are the unputs
{
  closure <- sort(unique(start_attrs)) #inializes the closure with the attributes we already know
  #ie. Closure for A+ = {A}
  changed <- TRUE #tells the algorithm whether we should continue looping 
  while (changed) {
    changed <- FALSE #at the beginning of each iteration, reset changed to FALSE assuming no new attributes will be added during this pass
    #if it finds the FD that adds a new attribute, it sets changed back to TRUE 
    fds <- dbReadTable(PSTAT132db, fd_table) #reading FDs from SQLite
    #loops through every functional dependency
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(fds))){
      U <- fds$lhs[i] #determinant
      V <- fds$rhs[i] #dependent attribute
      #If U subseteq X+, then set X+ = X+ union V
      if(U %in% closure && !(V %in% closure)) { #if the determinant is already in the closure and the dependent attribute is not already in the closure, 
        closure <- sort(c(closure, V))
        changed <- TRUE #something changed, loop again
      }
    }
  }
  return(closure)
  #Step 3: Terminate- no FD can add anything further closure
}
```

Running the Closure for A
A+ = the set of all attributes you can determine from A using the functional dependencies
```{r}
all_attrs <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")

#A+ Should contain A B C and D
A_plus <- attribute_closure(
  PSTAT132db, "FDs", "A", all_attrs
)

#printing results
cat("A+ =", paste(A_plus, collapse = ", "), "\n")

#Tesitng whether A is a superkey
is_superkey <- setequal(A_plus, all_attrs)
#setequal() checks whether A_plus contains exactly the same attributes as all_attrs
cat("Is A a superkey? ", ifelse(is_superkey, "YES", "NO"), "\n")
```

Calculating B+ for Comparison
Should start with {B}, then apply B -> C, giving {B, C} and then C -> D, giving {B, C, D}
```{r}
B_plus <- attribute_closure (PSTAT132db, "FDs", "B", all_attrs)
#Same function call as before, except the starting attribute is now B

cat("B+ =", paste(B_plus, collapse = ", "), "\n")

#Is B a superkey? 
#Expected Output: NO 
cat("Is B a superkey? ", ifelse(setequal(B_plus, all_attrs), "YES", "NO"), "\n")

#Verify relation using SQL 
#Verify that the table was successfully stored in SQLite and can be retrieved 
cat("\n Sample rows of R read back from SQLite:\n")
print(dbGetQuery(PSTAT132db, "SELECT * FROM R ORDER BY A"))

#Disconnectig from the database 
dbDisconnect(PSTAT132db)
```
